venue: Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, Florida, USA

analysis.summary: Norway face England in a quarter-final that pits the tournament's most prolific individual striker — Erling Haaland, 7 goals in 4 games at 39% conversion — against the best defensive record among the remaining sides (England have conceded just 5 goals in 5 games, 1.0 per match). Norway are historic quarter-finalists for the first time, having eliminated Brazil 2-1 in the Round of 16, while England won all five of their matches in regulation and overtime, including a dramatic 3-2 comeback against Mexico. England are heavily favoured but face real threat through Haaland and an exposed right-back channel caused by suspension and injury.
analysis.home_form: Norway finished Group I runners-up behind France: W vs Iraq 4-1 (Boston, Jun 17), W vs Senegal 3-2 (New York, Jun 23), L vs France 1-4 (Boston, Jun 26). Knockout stage: W vs Côte d'Ivoire 2-1 (Dallas, Jun 30), W vs Brazil 2-1 (New York, Jul 5). Overall: 4W 1L, 12 scored, 9 conceded (2.4 scored / 1.8 conceded per game). Haaland has scored 7 of Norway's 12 goals (58% share) and netted in 14 consecutive international matches. Norway have not kept a single clean sheet across all five tournament games. A squad-wide sickness bug has been reported in Norway's camp in the days before this fixture.
analysis.away_form: England topped Group L unbeaten: W vs Croatia 4-2 (Jun 17), D vs Ghana 0-0 (Jun 23), W vs Panama 2-0 (Jun 27). Knockout stage: W vs DR Congo 2-1 (Jul 1), W vs Mexico 3-2 (Jul 6). Overall: 4W 1D, 11 scored, 5 conceded (2.2 scored / 1.0 conceded per game; two clean sheets). Under Thomas Tuchel, England have shown tactical flexibility: high-possession (79% vs Ghana) but equally effective on the counter (33.2% possession yet won 3-2 vs Mexico). Jude Bellingham scored twice vs Mexico; Harry Kane has 3 tournament goals. England have the best defensive record of any remaining quarter-finalist.
analysis.h2h: England hold the overall career advantage across all senior meetings. Historically England dominated early fixtures (6-0 in 1937 through multiple one-sided results to 1980). Norway's two competitive wins were both in World Cup qualifiers: 2-1 in 1981 and 2-0 in 1993. The last meeting was a friendly in September 2014, England winning 1-0. The two nations have never previously met at the World Cup, making this a first-ever competitive knockout encounter between them.
injuries_news: England: Jarell Quansah suspended for two matches after receiving a red card (serious foul play) against Mexico — misses both QF and potential SF.
England: Reece James has not featured since the 0-0 draw with Ghana on June 23 due to a hamstring injury; his participation in this match is in serious doubt.
England: Jordan Henderson (wrist surgery following celebration injury vs Mexico) has been ruled out of the remainder of the tournament.
Norway: David Møller Wolfe was forced off against Brazil; fitness for this match is a concern but unconfirmed.
Norway: Multiple players reportedly affected by a sickness bug in the squad in the days leading up to kick-off (unconfirmed severity).
key_factors: Haaland threat vs England's CB pairing: Quansah's suspension forces Tuchel to rely on Stones and Guéhi as his centre-back pair. Haaland has a conversion rate of 39% on shots at WC 2026; containing his limited but deadly appearances in the box is the defining tactical challenge.

England's exposed right-back: With Quansah suspended and Reece James doubtful with hamstring trouble, England's right flank is vulnerable. Norway's wide players (including Andreas Schjelderup) may target this channel.

Norway's defensive fragility: Norway have conceded in every one of their five tournament matches and rank last among QF teams for goals conceded per game (1.8). England's multi-threat attack (Bellingham, Kane, Saka, Gordon) should create consistent opportunities.

Counter-attack vs possession: Norway will likely sit deep and funnel the ball to Haaland on the break. England under Tuchel have shown they can win both ways — through press-heavy possession and on the counter — but will be cautious about over-committing and leaving space for Haaland.
Miami July heat: Hard Rock Stadium in Miami in mid-July is extremely hot and humid. Fitness levels matter; Norway's reported squad illness could compound fatigue in the second half.
Norway one match fresher: Norway played their R16 on July 5 (6 days rest) vs England's July 6 R16 win (5 days rest). Marginal advantage to Norway on recovery.

value_notes: The supplied h2h odds (home 4.10, draw 3.70, away 1.87) are standard 90-minute market lines. Normalising to remove the 4.9% overround yields: Norway 23.3%, Draw 25.7%, England 51.0%. Converting these to full knockout-match (after ET) probabilities — splitting the draw probability evenly between ET/pens outcomes (50/50 assumption) — implies Norway advances ~36%, England advances ~64%. My model places England at 73% to advance, a 9-point uplift over the converted market, exceeding the 0.05 value threshold. This is grounded in: (1) England's significantly superior defensive record (1.0 goals conceded/game vs Norway's 1.8, the worst of any QF side); (2) Norway's heavy reliance on Haaland (58% of their goals) making their attack one-dimensional and manageable if neutralised; (3) Norway's pre-match sickness disruption. Selection with edge ≥ 0.05: England to advance (away h2h). For totals_2.5_over, my model (63%) exceeds market implied (1/1.70 = 58.8%), edge ~4.2% — marginal, below 0.05 threshold.
